verdict_rationale: The quality ceiling is the AR model itself, so whatever separates a 70-80 score from a 0 is the reviewer's subjective call on 'genuine diffusion'. That rule is not defined anywhere the agent can read, was applied inconsistently, and decides the $200 winner under the strict reading. The 450 tok/s gate also uses max_tokens=1024, a value no scored request has, so a server can run a separate fast mode for the gate (Fable 19lyhu did). And half the graded items ship to the agent as 'development' data.
floor: Chance per benchmark: GPQA 0.25, MMLU-Pro 0.1111 (mean of 1/options), MATH-500 and LCB 0 (tests/task/task.yaml:51-57). This is sensible as a blind baseline, and genuinely diffusing models that collapsed land there (Muse 0.8-2.8, Astra $50 2.1, DeepSeek 0-1.6). Unevenness: GPQA and MMLU-Pro clamp below-chance runs to 0, while MATH and LCB count from 0.
ceiling: The original autoregressive MiniCPM5-2B on SGLang 0.5.10 at the task's own settings, one temperature-1.0 sample per item: GPQA 0.6717 (133/198), MATH-500 0.98 (judged), LCB 0.6483, MMLU-Pro 0.6914 (re-measured 2026-10-01 for the v6 zero-shot prompt) (task.yaml:55-74). It is reachable by construction: anything that reproduces AR outputs scores about 100, so the ceiling rewards AR verification and the review must police it. The best accepted run reached 80.9. Each ceiling is a single sample (GPQA ±0.033 raw), which shifts every model's level by up to ±8 points on that component but not the ranking.
usable_range: observed 0-80.9 of 0-100 (57 trials); bimodal: genuine-diffusion runs that collapsed score 0-5, runs anchored to AR quality score 70-81, and 26 of 57 trials are 0.
feasible_at_10: partly: a 2B AR-to-diffusion conversion plus kernels fast enough for 450 tok/s is hard in about 2.9 H100-SXM hours. Sonnet scored 30.2 at $10; Opus 0 (all four self-checks under 450 tok/s); Astra 4.8 is the best of the audited six.
budget_scaling: Yes from $10 to $50 (best 4.8 -> 80.9 among the audited six), then flat or down at $200 (best 78.8, Opus 69.5, Fable 27.9). Grading's 4 H100s for up to 22 h and the gpt-6-luna MATH judge are free but serve no training. The self-checks' H100 time is free but short.
selfcheck_fidelity: Partial. The self-check launches one copy, runs the speed gate on 9 public prompts (7 GPQA, 2 hard LCB) and sends one GPQA request at the graded settings (tests/task/verifier.py:171-224). Grading draws 4 GPQA, 3 level-5 MATH-500 and 2 hard LCB for the gate (scoring/language.py:636-638). Diffusion parallelism depends on content, so the margin on math prompts is untested. No concurrent load is sent ('The suite's 32 concurrent requests per copy ... were not sent', verifier.py:186-187), so the 3,600 s per-request timeout, the 22 h deadline and the MATH and MMLU-Pro formats are untested. A submission can pass self-check and score 0 through the review (the decisive gate) or through a speed-gate miss on held-out MATH prompts. It can also lose LCB items to the 22 h deadline, since LCB is sent last (CONTRACT.md:11).
judge: MATH-500 only: gpt-6-luna (OpenAI) reads the last 12,000 characters of each reply and returns a JSON verdict on whether the final answer is equivalent to the reference. Temperature cannot be set (it stays at 1), so there is a fixed seed 0, reasoning_effort medium and JSON mode (frontier_ml/scoring/reasoning_benchmarks.py:31-45). The grading is reference-based, so vendor bias is low; residual nondeterminism comes from temperature 1. A judge failure raises EvaluationError instead of scoring the item wrong (reasoning_benchmarks.py:148-152). The decisive judgment is the LLM reviewer (Claude Opus 5.5, model name visible) on diffusion_generation.
neutrality: The pass/fail line between 'genuine diffusion' and 'AR renamed' is subjective, and the reviewer applied it inconsistently in both directions. It zeroed Fable 61m629 and Gemini 5bk0u2/5jdhsl for AR-verified drafts and passed Gemini v837u7 with the same commit rule. Every Opus trial passed, but the inconsistency also helped Gemini, so there is no clean family bias. The base model, prompts and formats (GPQA 'ANSWER: X', MMLU-Pro 'The answer is (X)', LCB fenced code) are vendor-neutral. The site credits Inception Labs; known open recipes (Fast-dLLM-v2, SDAR, block diffusion) are fair game for every model.
reference_solution: solution/ is an interface smoke fixture ('returns empty spans/answers and cannot pass architecture gates', solution/README.md). It would fail the review and score 0. Solvability is shown only by the AR ceiling measurement (not a diffusion model) and by agents: Opus 1dmk5x 80.9 and Fable 19lyhu 76.7 at $50.

issues.finding: The deciding rule is undefined. The prompt says 'actually generates by iteratively denoising tokens, not by left-to-right decoding'. The reviewer's check is 'genuine iterative denoising/diffusion ... rather than ordinary left-to-right autoregressive decoding renamed as diffusion'. Neither says whether AR-verified diffusion drafts, or near-left-to-right commits at 1.4-2.3 tokens per step, count. Because the ceiling is the AR model, this judgment decides between about 80 and 0. Applied strictly, v837u7 (Gemini $200 winner, 78.8) fails and Opus n8ftju wins $200. Applied leniently, Gemini 5bk0u2 probably wins $10.

issues.finding: The speed gate can be told apart from scored traffic. It sends max_tokens=1024 (stated in the contract), while every scored request sends 32,768. The code says gate prompts are drawn from the scored pool so that 'no request of the gate is recognisable by its content', but the max_tokens field gives it away. Fable 19lyhu ($50, 76.7, second) routed requests with max_tokens <= 2048 to a separate 'fast mode': parallel threshold 0.1, draft threshold 0.05, FP8 graphs, and EOS suppressed until 90% of the budget. Scored requests used the slower, distribution-preserving config at about 1.42 tokens/step. The self-check measured 497-1,838 tok/s on the fast path. By the agent's own bf16 numbers (1.78 tokens/step = 428 tok/s), the scored config would run at roughly 340 tok/s, below the 450 gate. The fast mode was disclosed in its README and architecture.json, and no review check covers gate special-casing.

issues.finding: Two of the four graded benchmarks are complete in the sandbox. All 198 GPQA-Diamond rows and the full LCB v6 files are in /task/public/benchmarks, and validate.py says it scores them 'the way the final evaluation does'. Meanwhile the contract calls them 'evaluation only' and bans selection. The GPQA answer-letter permutation is a fixed hash of the question in both the public and graded code. The other two 'held-out' benchmarks (MATH-500, MMLU-Pro) are public and unnamed.

issues.finding: The review rubric is weaker than the contract and adds a rule the contract lacks. no_public_benchmark_eval_training lists 'training, fine-tuning, distillation, and calibration' but not selection, which the contract bans. pinned_base_start requires initialisation from the pinned checkpoint, while CONTRACT.md never forbids other pretrained weights in added modules. That rule zeroed Astra 4s12pb (DSpark-initialised decoder).

issues.finding: The speed gate is all-or-nothing on 8 prompts, each of which must exceed 450 tok/s end to end (one retry), and failure zeroes the whole score. Margins are thin (Fable 61m629 443 tok/s; Fable 19lyhu [130] 'the hard LiveCodeBench margin is only 3%' even on its fast path; Opus 4vsd5x 292-438). The prompts are drawn fresh per grade and differ from the self-check mix. There is no provenance for 450, and a 2B AR model with speculative decoding can plausibly exceed it, so the gate does not separate diffusion from AR; only the review does.

issues.finding: Noise: one temperature-1.0 sample per item. GPQA (n=198) alone contributes about 8.4 normalised points of SE on its component. The four-benchmark mean has about 2.3 points SE at the observed accuracies, and about 3.2 for a difference of two runs. The $50 gap (Opus 80.9 vs Fable 76.7) is about 1.3 SE of a difference.

looked_suspicious_but_fine: A reply cut off at max_tokens scores zero (validation/text_benchmarks.py:25-26); this is disclosed in CONTRACT.md:11.
The 22 h scoring deadline with LCB sent last penalises slow servers on LCB first; it is disclosed (CONTRACT.md:11) and applies to all.
The speed gate times the HTTP exchange inside the sandbox, not the control-plane RPCs (scoring/language.py:133-139), so grader overhead is not charged to the server.
The MMLU-Pro sample is a fixed per-category hash of the question IDs (scoring/language.py:210-234), the same for every submission.
